title: Building an MCP Client: Discovery, Routing, and Dual-Era Fallback
service: multipeer: a multi-server MCP client host with routing and id correlation, an INI file of pinned peers, the stdio era probe, a crash-tolerant stdio pool and a collision-safe namespace merge

parts.lesson_anchor: Modern discovery (highest mutually supported version); Routing a call (local name, matching response id); Discovering and caching tools (missing legacy resultType is complete); code/main.py _mutual_version, call, decode_rpc_response
planted_bugs: protocol.mutual_version returns the first shared version in the peer's order, not the highest; discover succeeds and the wrong version shows up two calls later in a tools/call _meta

MultiServerClient.call sends the canonical name (notes/search) instead of the local name the owning peer declared; a gateway peer's local name notes/search also rules out cutting the canonical name at its last '/'
MultiServerClient._result demands resultType from every era, so a legacy peer's result raises ProtocolError
PendingCalls keeps a list: add scans it for duplicates and resolve scans it for the id, O(n) each
parts.timing_assert: 5000 adds plus 5000 shuffled resolves under 0.1 s (the scanning table takes about 1.5 s, the indexed one about 2 ms)
parts.overfix_guard: a modern result without resultType still raises, which rules out dropping the check or defaulting it for every era, and the legacy peer is on 2024-11-05, which rules out spotting legacy by the 2025-11-25 string; answers with id true, 1.0, null or [1] match nothing, the string '1' and the integer 1 stay apart, and a rejected answer leaves request 1 pending, which rules out a dict keyed by the bare id or by str(id) and popping before comparing types
parts.deviation: mutual_version lives in protocol.py, where the client's modern discovery, Part 3's negotiate and Part 4's pool all use it, and correlation is a PendingCalls class that the Part 4 pool reuses. The legacy peer gets its Selection directly, because choosing the era is Part 3's work and is not implemented in the starter. The bool-id guard also covers 1.0, null, an unhashable id, '1' against 1, and keeping the real request after a rejected answer.

parts.lesson_anchor: Allowlisting is operator intent, not evidence: allow_legacy bound to one pinned command or endpoint, no wildcard; Legacy is a compatibility branch: the era cache is discarded when the transport restarts; skill: pinned command or endpoint, arguments, explicit allow_legacy defaulting to false
parts.exactness: save then load returns the same PeerConfig list in the same order: argv with quotes, an empty argument, padded spaces, %, # and ; survives through shlex, % in endpoints stays literal, booleans and integers come back typed, tuples stay tuples; an operator-written file with yes/off, %PORT% and shell quoting loads as written
traps: BasicInterpolation on load (InterpolationSyntaxError) or on save (invalid interpolation syntax)
argv split on whitespace or joined with spaces
both or neither of argv and endpoint
[DEFAULT] sidestepped by renaming default_section, so it loads as a peer
parts.deviation: The suggested trap 'configparser lowercases keys' cannot fire here: every key is a fixed lowercase name and peer names sit in section headers, which configparser keeps as written. It became a follow-up question about storing an environment allowlist as keys. The DEFAULT-section wildcard, duplicate sections and the silently skipped missing file took its place. The era cache not being persisted is a clarifying question, not an assertion.

parts.lesson_anchor: The stdio compatibility probe (three outcome classes, -32020/-32021/-32022, -32601 is not evidence); Allowlisting is operator intent (one bounded initialize, five checks); Legacy is a compatibility branch (notifications/initialized only after every check)
traps: recognized modern error downgraded for an allowlisted peer
-32022 with no common version falling back to initialize
empty answer not treated as silence
revision compared with the built-in constant
initialize under the discovery timeout or with _meta
serverInfo name checked for truthiness, not type
clarifying_questions: a discovery answer with the wrong id
parts.deviation: The bool-id trap is not repeated here, since Part 1 has it and lesson 07's exam has another; the initialize answer is checked against another request's id instead.

parts.lesson_anchor: Routing a call: do not send on an unavailable transport; reconnect or restart, re-run discovery and tools/list, retry with a new id when the safety policy permits; Legacy is a compatibility branch: discard the era cache when the transport restarts; skill: fail in-flight work, retry only operations allowed by the safety policy
parts.wire_format: newline-delimited JSON-RPC written to each peer's stdin, decided by the test's split(b'\n') and json.loads per line; the fake peers also parse every line as it arrives
traps: calls serialized (write one, wait for its answer)
in-flight calls left waiting when the process exits
cached era kept across a restart
no rediscovery or relisting before the retry
per-process id counters reusing the lost call's id
a slow peer blocking the others
answers matched to the oldest pending call instead of by id
retry_safe merged across peers (restore is safe on files, not on notes)
parts.deviation: Pool peers are modern only, because the legacy branch is Part 3's work. The dropped era cache shows up as a restarted process that supports a newer version. Added: one retry only (a peer that dies twice), and a call after a crash restarts the peer.

parts.lesson_anchor: Collision-safe namespace merge (prefix on collision, reject on collision, never silent overwrite, store canonical and local names); Discovering and caching tools: sort before merging so registry order does not depend on startup timing
traps: connection order decides the bare name
a gateway's local names with '/' taken as bare names, so a prefixed name collides (the lesson code raises) or overwrites
an error naming only one peer
a name listed twice by one peer prefixed or deduplicated
a '/' name prefixed only when it starts with a known peer name
parts.integration: 300 seeded random catalogs: every (peer, tool) gets exactly one canonical name, and every canonical name splits back into its peer and local name
clarifying_questions: first or all collisions in the error
parts.deviation: Added the peer-name rule and the randomized injectivity check; the nesting is a gateway peer whose local names are themselves namespaced.
